A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ESWM research. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original prediction, representation, exploration, navigation, and adaptation experiments in simulated environments, including MiniGrid results in Figure A9.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds ProcThor experiments, TEM-T comparisons, robustness tests, and additional quantitative analyses.

M1.justification: V2 adds a substantial ProcThor adaptation using DINOv3 features, 33 tokens per transition, alternating within-transition/global attention, and cosine-distance state loss (Appendix C.1.4–C.1.5). It also introduces trajectory-conditioned queries for duplicate states and changes the described LSTM/Mamba input from a terminal query token to query-conditioned memory tokens. The core episodic prediction and planning procedures remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds ProcThor indoor scenes with first-person RGB observations and continuous displacement/rotation inputs, extending beyond v1's grid environments. It also evaluates duplicate-state environments and contradictory memories. MiniGrid was already evaluated in v1 Figure A9 and is not an entirely new benchmark.

E2.justification: V2 introduces TEM-T as an evaluated world-model comparator in Open Arena and Random Wall, including the non-minimal-memory comparison (Figures 2 and 9). This substantially expands the direct comparison with related spatial-memory models. EPN, EMWM, LSTM, and Mamba comparisons already existed in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include minimal spanning trajectories for TEM-T, ESWM controls trained on that trajectory distribution, and ProcThor evaluation using discretized action classes and state-feature cosine similarity. Figure 4c changes from a four-layer to a twelve-layer transformer and extends the memory-size sweep to partial-coverage settings. Figure 2 also revises evaluated model depths.

E4.justification: V2 adds attention-head and training-minimality ablations, controls separating TEM-T architecture from training distribution, trained-versus-untrained sRSA analysis, and noise and environment-size generalization tests. The EPN small-memory ablation in v1 Figure A6 is removed. Disconnected-memory and guided-planning analyses are retained after relocation to Appendix D.

E5.justification: V1 Figure A6 displays three individual EPN seeds; v2 Figure 15 reports four-seed means and standard deviations for both ESWM and EPN, with Welch tests. V2 also discloses best-seed selection for Figure 5 and identifies Figure 4a's uncertainty bands as 95% confidence intervals. These substantially change uncertainty reporting without establishing that every experiment received additional runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds ProcThor predictions, query-type accuracy tables, and numerous ablation and robustness outcomes, including trained/untrained sRSA of 0.78 ± 0.02 versus 0.50 ± 0.04. Exploration coverage is revised from 90% to 91 ± 2%. Figures 2 and 4c contain replaced results under revised model configurations, so they do not establish matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The core mathematical formulation, environment definitions, latent-distance heuristic construction, and admissibility discussion are retained. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. The added minimality experiments and standard sRSA metric concern empirical settings and analysis rather than new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about episodic spatial inference, emergent maps, adaptation, and navigation remain. V2 adds scalability to realistic continuous environments with high-dimensional inputs as an explicit main contribution. V1 presents only preliminary MiniGrid evidence and leaves more realistic sensory environments primarily to future work.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for TEM-T's performance gap and the benefits of minimal-memory training, and revises the Open Arena failure discussion toward overfitting. It explicitly identifies ambiguity from duplicate states without historical context. The limitations discussion shifts from simplified sensory/action representations toward remaining challenges in physical robotic navigation.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's limited MiniGrid documentation, v2 specifies its object encoding and prediction heads. It also documents ProcThor sampling, DINOv3 processing, attention architecture, and training resources, including four A100 GPUs for 80,000 iterations over 19 days. Custom TEM-T implementation and sRSA/noise-analysis procedures provide substantial additional reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning against GTM-SM, TEM, successor representations, and recurrent predictive models. New Appendix B develops the biological evidence for integrating disjoint experiences through additional cited studies. ProcThor, DINOv3, and VGGT references support the new extension; existing TEM citations are developed rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and substantial portions of related work, methods, and interpretation. It moves disconnected-memory analysis and guided imagination from the main text into Appendix D, restructures the experimental narrative around scalability, and reorganizes the appendices. These are substantial narrative changes beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds four tables and Figures 7–9, expands MiniGrid into the combined MiniGrid/ProcThor Figure 6, and redraws Figures 2 and 4. Figure A6 becomes a redesigned four-seed comparison in Figure 15. Other appendix figures are largely retained and renumbered, alongside the document-wide conference-format change.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for generalization and memory-based reasoning through ProcThor experiments, a relevant TEM-T comparison with distribution controls, and targeted robustness and ablation tests. Four-seed ESWM/EPN reporting and fuller implementation details address important validation and reproducibility gaps in v1. ProcThor remains preliminary simulation evidence, and the EPN memory-size ablation is lost, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential strength.
